expressions.example: My phone ran out of battery at four.
I got lost in New York.
A woman lent me her power bank.
What’s the address of the restaurant?
By then, it was eight o’clock.

expressions.pt: no fim, depois de algum tempo

dialogue.g: E aí, como foi Nova York?

dialogue.text: Pretty good, but on the second day, my phone died at four in the afternoon.
dialogue.g: Bem bom, mas no segundo dia o meu celular descarregou às quatro da tarde.

dialogue.text: I’d been using it as a map all day, and I didn’t notice how low the battery was. And I’d left my charger at the hotel.
dialogue.g: Eu vinha usando o celular como mapa o dia todo, e não reparei na bateria. E tinha deixado o carregador no hotel.

dialogue.text: Why didn’t you go back to the hotel?
dialogue.g: Por que você não voltou para o hotel?

dialogue.text: I tried, but I got lost. And the team dinner was at seven. The address was in a message from Raj!
dialogue.g: Eu tentei, mas me perdi. E o jantar da equipe era às sete. O endereço estava numa mensagem do Raj!
E aí, o que você fez?

dialogue.text: I asked a doorman for help, and he told me about a café. But there were no free outlets.
dialogue.g: Pedi ajuda a um porteiro, e ele me falou de um café. Mas não tinha nenhuma tomada livre.

dialogue.text: I’d been waiting there alone for twenty minutes when a woman lent me her power bank. Luckily, I had my cable.
dialogue.g: Eu estava esperando lá sozinha havia vinte minutos quando uma moça me emprestou a bateria portátil dela. Por sorte, eu estava com o meu cabo.

dialogue.text: So did you make it to the dinner?
dialogue.g: E você chegou ao jantar, afinal?

dialogue.text: Eventually, yes. I caught a taxi and got there at eight. By then, they’d been waiting for an hour!
dialogue.g: No fim, sim. Peguei um táxi e cheguei às oito. Àquela altura, eles já estavam esperando havia uma hora!

grammar.question: Activity before that point
grammar.example: I’d been using it as a map all day.

grammar.question: An earlier completed action
grammar.example: I’d left my charger at the hotel.

grammar.question: In progress at that moment
grammar.example: I was walking when my phone died.

listeningStatements.text: The team waited at the door for an hour.
listeningStatements.correction: No. For fifteen minutes. Then they got a table.
Yes. He called her three times.

listeningStatements.text: Sarah thinks Ana is at the hotel.
listeningStatements.correction: No. She thinks Ana got lost in Times Square.

listeningStatements.text: They didn’t order any food for Ana.
listeningStatements.correction: No. They ordered a pizza for her.

corrections.s: I was walking since two o’clock when my phone died.
corrections.a: I’d been walking since two o’clock when my phone died.
corrections.why: Use had been + -ing for an activity continuing before another past event.
corrections.pre: Describe an activity continuing up to a past event.

corrections.s: Can you borrow me your charger?
corrections.a: Can you lend me your charger?
corrections.why: Lend means give temporarily; borrow means take temporarily. Can I borrow your charger? also works.
corrections.pre: Ask to use someone else’s charger.

corrections.s: I’d been waiting for twenty minutes when a woman lent me her power bank.
corrections.a: I’d been waiting for twenty minutes when a woman lent me her power bank.
corrections.why: The continuous describes the earlier waiting; the simple past gives the event that interrupted it.
corrections.pre: Describe waiting before someone offered help.

corrections.why: Get lost describes being unable to find your way. Lose yourself has other, often figurative meanings.
corrections.pre: Explain that you could not find your way back.

corrections.s: Eventually my phone dies, maybe once a month.
corrections.a: Sometimes my phone dies, maybe once a month.
corrections.why: Eventually means in the end. Sometimes describes frequency.
corrections.pre: Describe something that happens from time to time.

listening.transcript: Hi Ana, it’s Raj. It’s seven twenty. We’d been waiting for you at the door for fifteen minutes, so we got a table. I’ve called you three times, but no answer! Sarah thinks you got lost in Times Square. The food here is pretty good, so we ordered a pizza for you. You need a power bank, Ana! Call me when you get this, or just come straight to the restaurant, OK?
